frontmatter.title: Amman Mineral: the operating turn is real, the copper marker is the valuation
frontmatter.summary: We stay at HOLD with a target of Rp3,660, a total return of 1.9%. The third quarter confirmed the integrated turn: unit costs fell, by-product credits covered them and net debt came down. We hold the volume path at the guided run-rate and carry the gold credit through realisation. At the reviewed copper marker the shares are about fairly priced; the Elang build absorbs the cash.
thesis: Gold is close to half of the price we receive per tonne of copper at the marker ratio, so the gold credit is the second value driver; it enters through 1.97x realisation, not a separate revenue line.

The 2026 sales shortfall is inventory timing, not a mine problem; we normalise copper sales to the 220 kt run-rate and hold them to the Elang handover, because Batu Hijau stockpiles are processed until 2033/34 [S3 p.19, F23].
The third quarter confirmed the operating turn, with unit operating costs of 2.19 a pound, by-product credits of 4.78 and net debt of US$4,998 [S3 p.11, p.14, p.21].
Elang reuses the smelter, plant, power and port, so the build is a mine and a conveyor; we still charge a capital overrun in the bear.
The company pays no dividend until the build completes, so the equity holder waits for cash return while the interest bill runs at US$386.
The base case is close to the share price; copper at the marker, not gold, is what decides the rating.

blocks.text: We stay at HOLD with a target of Rp3,660 against a share price of Rp3,590, a total return of 1.9% over twelve months [S2 p.48, S3 p.6]. The life-of-asset NAV is Rp3,496 per share; the base case is Rp3,997, the bull Rp5,832 and the bear Rp814, and the probability-weighted target Rp3,660 [S6].

This is a results revision, not a new view of copper. The third-quarter LK is now in the model: nine-month sales of US$3,238, EBITDA of US$1,833 and net income of US$880 [S3 p.6]. The bear now carries the project risk as a twenty per cent capital overrun rather than a permanent volume cut, and the gold shock is a five per cent move in the whole realisation ratio - roughly a tenth off the gold credit and the same five per cent off the copper credit - with the bull as its mirror [S6, S3 p.14].

The quarter was the cleanest read yet: net sales US$1,185, EBITDA US$705, net income US$376, unit operating costs 2.19 a pound and by-product credits 4.78 a pound, which carried the net cash cost below zero [S3 p.11, p.14, p.15]. Nine-month operating cash flow turned to US$839 from an outflow a year earlier, capital expenditure fell to US$170 and net debt came down to US$4,998 [S3 p.6, p.12, p.21]. That is the operating turn the base case already carried, now confirmed in the accounts.

The call is still the copper marker. The reviewed through-cycle price is US$11,000/t against a spot print of US$13,924/t [S2 p.101, S3 p.6]. At the marker the equity is worth about what it trades at: the base case is Rp3,997 against Rp3,590, and only copper holding today's print produces the bull case's Rp5,832 [S2 p.101]. Gold does the rest of the work through the by-product credit, which is why we carry the realisation ratio rather than a separate gold line [S3 p.14, S6].

We do not book the inventory unwind as a second gain. Gold sold per tonne of copper is carried at the nine-month actual mix, 1.80x realisation, not at the raised 775 koz gold-in-concentrate guidance, because the gap is inventory: the company produced 195 koz in the third quarter and sold only a fraction of it [S3 p.7, p.18, F31]. We also carry no dividend until the Elang build completes, per the LK [S2 p.107].

AMMN owns Batu Hijau and is developing Elang, both in West Sumbawa Regency, West Nusa Tenggara [S2 p.48]. It holds almost all of PT Amman Mineral Nusa Tenggara, which holds the mining licence and runs the chain from pit to cathode and refined gold [S2 p.48].

The business has changed shape: AMMN now sells copper cathode, refined gold, refined silver and sulphuric acid as well as concentrate [S2 p.52, S4 p.5]. The smelter and precious-metals refinery are built for an annual output of up to 220 kt of copper cathode and 579 koz of refined gold from 900 kt of concentrate input [S3 p.13, F60, F61]. The integration captures the downstream margin and satisfies Indonesia's domestic-processing requirement [S2 p.52, S3 p.5].

The third quarter is the first clean read on the integration. The smelter and refinery passed their performance guarantee test, producing 54.0 kt of cathode and 55.9 koz of refined gold in the quarter, which remains below the refinery's 579 koz design output and reflects smelter input grade and blending rather than a design-capacity run-rate [S3 p.10, p.12, F60, F61]. The mine produced 121 Mlbs of copper and 195 koz of gold in concentrate in the same three months, so contained metal accumulated in stockpile rather than being sold [S3 p.9, F31]. That is a timing feature of a chain whose refining capacity is smaller than its mining capacity, not a demand problem [S3 p.7].

The growth plan has two legs: the concentrator, expanded to 85 million tonnes a year with first ore in mid-August, and Elang, where the definitive study is complete, the owner's cost tender is running and final investment decision is targeted for 2027 with first ore after Batu Hijau's mine life [S3 p.5, p.12, S5, S6]. Batu Hijau's reserve is 777 million tonnes of ore and Elang's reserve contains 8,242 kt of copper with a gold credit that changes the revenue mix when it enters the plan [S6, S3 p.23].

Ownership is concentrated: PT Sumber Gemilang Persada holds just under a third, Medco Energi about a fifth, PT AP Investment about a sixth, and the public under a fifth, with a free float of 22.8% [S2 p.48]. The company operates under a special mining business licence converted from the original contract of work and pays royalties on copper and gold; the schedule was raised in April of the last year, with copper cathode at a mid-single-digit to high-single-digit rate and gold in the high teens [S2 p.48, p.101].

Copper sets revenue, and the reviewed deck carries a through-cycle marker of US$11,000/t against spot US$13,924/t, a gap the desk treats as cyclical tightness rather than a new equilibrium [S2 p.101, S3 p.6]. Gold's marker is US$4,300/oz against spot US$4,126/oz, and silver is a small third credit [S2 p.101]. The reserve statement is struck at copper 4.00 a pound and gold 2,500 an ounce, below the deck marker; we value on the reviewed series and use the reserve price as the bear's anchor [S6].

The cost position is the moat. The company reports a negative adjusted unit cash cost after by-product credits, and the current-year figure is also negative [S2 p.91, S3 p.11]. A negative cash cost means gold, silver and acid credits cover the cash cost of copper, so the mine survives a price well below the marker [S2 p.91]. The advantage is not permanent: it depends on gold credits, diesel and power, and the strip ratio [S2 p.100].

Rivalry is global and disciplined by the cost curve, and copper has no close substitute at scale in electrical use [S2 p.101]. Buyer power sits with global traders and smelters, though the integrated smelter reduces treatment and refining exposure [S2 p.52]. Supplier power is real in diesel, power and consumables, and regulation is the binding constraint: royalties, export permits and the domestic-processing obligation are set by policy [S2 p.101, p.52].

The house macro frame is a balance-of-payments pressure regime with a cautious tilt, neutral on the commodity complex as a single beta, so the tilt neither favours nor penalises this name [S2 p.101]. The rupiah assumption is Rp18,350/USD to the dollar; a weaker rupiah raises the rupiah target mechanically without changing the dollar value of the business [S2 p.101].

The last full year was a transition year. Revenue was US$1,847, reported EBITDA US$1,057 and net profit US$249, below the prior year because volumes fell during the smelter ramp and interest costs rose [S2 p.98, S4 p.5]. The presentation EBITDA is higher than the income-statement build of US$921 because it adds back items the statutory accounts do not isolate; we use the lower figure so the forecast is not flattered [S2 p.100, S4 p.5].

Cost of revenue was US$1,011, of which royalties were US$219 and depreciation and amortisation US$247, leaving a cash cost that the model forecasts per tonne [S2 p.100, p.101]. The cash cost is gross of the gold and silver credits, which sit in the realisation ratio, so the two lines together reproduce the margin [S2 p.98]. The engine's calibration re-prices the current year at last year's copper and volume but with this year's by-product credit, so its positive gap is the gold mix, not a cost error [S2 p.100, F5, F17].

The current year is calibrated to reported actuals. Nine-month net sales were US$3,238, EBITDA US$1,833 and net income US$880, against our full-year forecasts of US$4,436, US$2,552 and US$1,199, so the fourth quarter is forecast broadly in line with the third rather than a collapse [S3 p.6, p.7]. Copper sold is 180 kt for the year because sales, not mine output, are the constraint: the company produced more concentrate than it sold while the smelter commissioned [S3 p.7, p.21].

We model copper sold recovering to 220 kt at the guided run-rate and holding 220 kt to the Elang handover, before Elang lifts the plateau to 238 kt [S2 p.107, S3 p.7, p.19, S6]. Nothing in the record retires a tonne before 2031/32, and Batu Hijau's stockpiles are processed until 2033/34 [S3 p.19, F23].

Net debt was US$4,998 at 30 September 2026, before the US$55 buy-back announced on 22 October: the buy-back post-dates the balance sheet, so it is not inside that figure and is deducted separately in the valuation bridge, while the nine months show the debt reduction the LK reports, with leverage below two times [S3 p.5, p.6]. The stockpile stood at US$2,680, up US$1,160 in nine months, so our working-capital build is the disclosed increase of US$1,133, not a release [S9, F31, F32]. The ratio then eases toward 36.0% of revenue by FY2030E as the stockpile converts over the Batu Hijau life [S3 p.19].

Capital expenditure is the largest judgement. The company has not published an Elang budget: the conveyor tender is in progress and final investment decision is targeted for 2027 [S3 p.19]. Recent outturn of US$1,373 in the last full year and US$1,792 the year before built the smelter and refinery that Elang reuses, so it is not a proxy [S2 p.104, S3 p.19]. We carry the build at US$7,000 per tonne of copper across FY2028E-FY2031E, our own mid-range assumption because no Elang budget is disclosed, and test a twenty per cent overrun in the bear [S3 p.19, S6]. The company pays no dividend until the programmes complete, then distributes 40.0% from FY2032E [S2 p.107].

Earnings quality carries three flags, all optics-class. The reported EBITDA is above the statutory build, which we resolve conservatively [S4 p.5, S2 p.100]. Operating cash flow was negative in the last full year on the working-capital build and smelter commissioning, and it turns positive as inventory unwinds [S8 p.76, S2 p.98]. Depreciation is low against capital spent, so statutory earnings may be flattered; the model uses disclosed depreciation per tonne, not extrapolated capex [S2 p.100, F5].

We value AMMN on a life-of-asset DCF, the method the commodity-producer card requires for a depleting asset [S6]. The target is one hundred per cent that DCF: no domestic copper peer benchmark exists for an EV/EBITDA cross-check, and P/BV is excluded because a mine's book value is a depreciating historical cost [S2 p.104].

The cost of capital is built from the house macro inputs [deck: macro]: risk-free 4.86%, mature equity risk premium 4.23%, Indonesia country risk premium 2.46%, unlevered beta 1.00, gearing 38.6%, levered beta 1.30, cost of equity 14.3% and WACC 11.8%. The rates and the country premium are the house macro inputs [deck: macro]; the beta is the house industry default for precious and base metals, not a company beta, because AMMN's own trading history is too short and too dominated by the 2023 listing and the 2026 index deletion to fit one. The company-specific evidence we have is the coupon and gearing of its debt [S2 p.101]. The pre-tax cost of debt in the build is 6.9%, below the high-single-digit coupon the accounts pay, so we add a company premium of under a percentage point to the cost of equity to hold the WACC at the level the company's own debt implies [S0, S2 p.102].

The orebody value is in the audited reserve statement: Elang's 17.8 billion pounds of contained copper at a gold grade of about three and a quarter ounces per tonne of contained copper [S2 p.88, p.93]. The DCF base is the combined JORC reserve: 8,242 kt of contained copper at Elang plus 2,608 kt at Batu Hijau, 10,850 kt in total [S3 p.23, F7, F53, F59]. At the plan's volume path the reserve is consumed inside the forecast window: FY2071E is the last full production year at the plateau, and the contained copper still in the ground when it closes is a rounding residual we value at nothing. That is why the window ends there and carries no terminal value - the value is the orebody the model mines, and nothing beyond the plan is assumed to exist [S6, F11, F59].

The result is an enterprise value of US$18,916. The bridge to equity deducts net debt of US$4,998 at 30 September 2026, minorities and the post-balance-sheet buy-back of US$55, and adds back the associates and investments carried on the balance sheet; the valuation table in this section prints each of those lines with its value, and the sum gives Rp3,496 per share [S0, S3 p.6, F22, F43]. The base-case target of Rp3,997 rolls that value forward at the cost of equity for the twelve-month horizon [S2 p.101].

The cross-checks are thin. The target is entirely the life-of-asset DCF against an industry default weight of six tenths; no peer multiple can carry the rest [S6, S2 p.104]. The market's own multiple is EV/EBITDA of 7.8 times for the current year and 6.9 times next, and P/BV of 2.2 times; those restate the price, they do not value the orebody [S2 p.101]. The anchor is NAV, not dividend capacity: no dividend is paid until the Elang build completes, so a dividend-capacity yield is not computable before FY2032E [S2 p.107].

The engine's sensitivity grid and reverse-DCF solver are keyed to the industry default gold deck rather than this model's copper driver, so neither moves value and we publish the scenario table in section five instead: a fifteen per cent cut to the marker and a twenty-five per cent uplift bracket the base, and the gold channel is a five per cent move in realisation either way [S2 p.101, S6, S3 p.14].

At the marker the equity is worth about what it trades at. The market pays Rp3,590 for an asset we value at Rp3,496, and the base case rolls to Rp3,997 [S2 p.48, S6]. The earlier premium was our own arithmetic - a by-product credit struck at the current-year ratio, an unsourced volume cut and a reserve life that stopped at Elang; corrected, there is no margin of safety [S2 p.101].

The first risk is copper. The share price is sensitive to a metal above its through-cycle marker, and a normalisation would take the equity below the base case [S2 p.101]. The bear case applies a fifteen per cent discount to the marker, a five per cent cut to the whole realisation ratio - roughly a tenth off the gold credit and the same five per cent off the copper credit - and a twenty per cent Elang capital overrun, with no volume cut because a schedule slip is timing, not a permanent loss of ore [S6, S3 p.14]. It produces Rp814, a positive equity value; the engine's limited-liability floor is not engaged at these shocks [S6].

The second risk is Elang execution. The project is not at final investment decision, the cost tender is running and the budget is undisclosed; we carry our own mid-range estimate and test a twenty per cent overrun in the bear [S3 p.5, p.19, S6]. A delay pushes cash flows right and raises the net debt carried through the build [S6]. Funding changes the debt/equity split, not enterprise value, so we add no financing case to the bull [S2 p.102].

The third risk is policy: royalties were raised in the last year, export permits are periodic and the domestic-processing obligation shapes the capital programme [S2 p.101, p.52]. The fourth is the smelter: the ramp has had repair-related downtime at the flash converting furnace and acid plant, and utilisation is the test of the integrated model [S2 p.52]. The fifth is the balance sheet: net debt is material against trough EBITDA, and the Elang build will consume cash while copper may be normalising [S3 p.6, S6].

The sixth risk is geological: Phase Eight grades, recovery and strip ratio determine the volume path, and a reconciliation shortfall would cut volume and raise unit cost at the same time [S2 p.107, S6]. The seventh is governance and liquidity: the register is concentrated, the free float is 22.8%, and a large shareholder transaction would move the price [S2 p.48]. The absence of a dividend means the minority depends on the controller's capital allocation [S2 p.107].

The scenario set has three drivers. The bear multiplies the copper deck by zero point eight five, the realisation ratio by zero point nine five and capex intensity by one point two; the bull multiplies the same drivers by one point two five, one point zero five and zero point eight three three [S6, S3 p.14]. The bear lands above the reserve price of 4.00 a pound and the bull stays below the US$13,924/t spot print, which is the copper asymmetry [S6, F28].

The probabilities are twenty-five per cent bear, fifty per cent base and twenty-five per cent bull. The base case is the through-cycle marker with the volume recovery and the Elang build, and it produces Rp3,997; the bear produces Rp814 and the bull Rp5,832. The bull is a marker re-set toward spot, not an extrapolation beyond it, and the bear is a severe but positive outcome rather than a wipe-out [S2 p.101, S6]. The weighted target is Rp3,660.

The signposts are specific. A sustained copper price above the marker moves us toward the bull; a break below it moves us toward the bear [S2 p.101]. The Elang final investment decision and cost-tender outcome are the next company catalysts [S3 p.5, S6]. Quarterly cathode output and unit cash cost are the operating tests, and the net-debt trajectory through the build is the balance-sheet test [S3 p.6, p.11]. We would revisit the rating on any of these before the next scheduled refresh [S6].

The register is concentrated: PT Sumber Gemilang Persada just over thirty per cent, Medco Energi about a fifth, PT AP Investment about a sixth, with smaller blocks and the public [S2 p.48]. The operating subsidiary is almost wholly owned, with a tiny residual held by PT AP Investment, a parent shareholder; that is common in Indonesian resource groups but means the minority should watch affiliate transactions [S2 p.48]. No disclosed related-party transaction changes the earnings picture, and there is no material related-party sales line [S2 p.14, p.15].

The board and audit arrangements are conventional for an IDX large cap: independent commissioners, an audit committee and the usual governance disclosures [S2]. The auditor's opinion is unqualified, with no restatement, qualification or material weakness in the record [S2]. We checked the listing status and found no special notation, unusual market activity notice, suspension or delisting warning in the archived record [S2].

On the accrual side, net profit exceeded free cash flow in each of the last two years: US$637 of attributable profit against US$-773 of free cash flow, and US$249 against US$-1,297, with a working-capital build of US$720 on top of US$132 [S2 p.98, S8 p.76]. The gap is timing and classification, not manipulation: the working capital is concentrate and refined metal awaiting sale, and the interest line absorbs the difference [S2 p.100, p.102]. We classify the accrual and working-capital flags as optics and the depreciation-timing flag as a conservatism we correct [S2 p.100, F5].

Capital returns are deferred: the company pays no dividend until its major programmes complete, and the buy-back is small relative to market capitalisation [S2 p.107, S3 p.5]. The environmental and social exposure is typical of a large copper-gold open pit: land disturbance, tailings, water, dust and smelter emissions, with rehabilitation and an LNG and combined-cycle power transition under way [S2 p.53]. Safety is the highest-tail social risk, and a serious incident would affect the licence and the production path at once; we treat it as a qualitative discount rather than a modelled scenario [S2 p.53].

The calendar is dominated by the Elang copper project: the owner's cost tender is in progress, the FID is targeted for the following year, and first ore is projected after Batu Hijau's mine life ends [S3 p.5, S6]. The tender sets the capital number our estimate proxies; a lower outcome would lift the middle years and a higher one would deepen the bear case [S6].

The operating catalysts are quarterly: the smelter and refinery passed their performance-guarantee test in the third quarter and the unit cash cost fell as by-product credits rose [S3 p.10, p.12]. Passing the test is not the same as running at nameplate — refined metal output remains well below the smelter's design capacity, and the expansion of the concentrator is still ramping [S5]. We watch the cathode and refined-gold output against the new guidance ranges rather than against nameplate, and the concentrate stockpile for evidence of sales timing [S3 p.18, F49, F50, F31]. The company says 2027 guidance will be released with the full-year report in the first quarter, the next scheduled input to the model [S3 p.18].

The financial catalysts are the full-year results and the debt trajectory: net debt fell as free cash flow was applied to repayment, and the question is whether that continues into the Elang build or reverses [S3 p.6]. The buy-back is a minor catalyst but a signal about management's view of the share price [S3 p.5, F22]. Policy catalysts are the royalty schedule, raised in the last year, and the periodic export permits; the market catalysts are copper and gold, with the share price more sensitive to copper than gold [S2 p.101].

The KPIs we monitor between updates are copper sold, cathode output, refined gold, unit cash cost, the strip ratio and grade, capital expenditure, net debt and the Elang tender outcome [S3 p.7, p.11, S6]. The model is refreshed when the full-year results or the Elang decision lands [S3 p.5].

bear.narrative: Both metals give back and the build lands over budget. Copper falls fifteen per cent below the 11,000/t deck marker to about US$9,350/t - still above the US$4.00/lb (US$8,818/t) price at which the company books its own reserve [S6, F28] - as Chinese property demand stays weak and Indonesian supply arrives, and the whole realisation ratio gives back five per cent: the gold credit falls by roughly a tenth and the copper and other credits fall by the same five per cent. The Elang owner's cost tender lands twenty per cent over our base assumption. The FID slip is a one-year timing shift, not a permanent loss of ore, so the volume path is held: the model's only project shock is the capital overrun, applied through capex intensity. No extra royalty or permit haircut is stacked: the royalty is the LK's effective rate [S2 p.101, F17] and the reserves and first-ore date are disclosed [S6].

bull.narrative: Spot persists, gold holds and the build goes right. Copper twenty-five per cent above the 11,000/t through-cycle marker is US$13,750/t against a US$13,924/t spot print, so the bull is a marker re-set rather than a number the tape already exceeds, and the deck's 4,300/oz gold marker holds with the whole realisation ratio five per cent higher - roughly a tenth added to the gold credit and the same five per cent to the copper and other credits. The expanded plant runs at nameplate, but we do not add a separate volume uplift because the base path already sits at the recovery-limited plateau; Elang's FID lands in 2027 with the mine and conveyor one-sixth under the base assumption, the reciprocal of the bear overrun. The upside is capped by the same effective royalty [S2 p.101, F17]; the capex underspend is not project financing, because the DCF is an enterprise valuation whose WACC already carries the modelled gearing [S2 p.102].

assumptions.label: Copper sales volume plan (kt Cu, all products)
assumptions.basis: The model is on copper metal sold, matching the LK's own sales metric. FY2026E 180 kt: 9M2026 copper sales were 98.3 kt of cathode plus 73 Mlbs (33.1 kt) of copper in concentrate = 131.4 kt, and Q3/Q4 sell refined metal only at about the Q3 cathode run-rate (50 kt in Q3), so the fourth quarter adds roughly 49 kt on the latest actual, not the 220 kt full-year production guidance [S3 p.7, p.14, p.21; S2 p.107, F11]. Inventory, not mine output, is the timing difference: 2025 ended with concentrate stockpiled ahead of the smelter and 9M2026 still built refined-metal inventory [S8 p.76, S3 p.21]. FY2027E 220 kt is the 2026 guidance run-rate at design smelter utilisation (220,000 t contained copper, F11); FY2028E-FY2031E hold 220 kt because nothing in the record retires it: Batu Hijau's mine life runs to 2031/2032 and its stockpiles are processed until 2033/2034+ [S3 p.19, F23], and 220 kt is the run-rate the company has just guided to. An earlier draft stepped the volume down to 195 and 170 kt in those years with no citation; that drift is withdrawn. FY2032E 225 kt introduces Elang first ore through the expanded 85 Mtpa concentrator [S5, F25]; the ceiling is physical, not a demand view: 85 Mt at the 0.319% Cu reserve grade [S6, F7] is 271 kt of contained copper, about 239 kt at 88% recovery, and blending higher-grade Batu Hijau stockpile ore lifts the plateau, so the base plateau is set at the recovery-limited 238 kt and the Elang ramp runs 225/232/236/238 kt in FY2032E-FY2035E. No volume shock is carried in either scenario: the ceiling is physical and both cases move copper price, realisation and capex intensity, so a volume uplift would double-count an upside the base path already holds. No bull volume add and no bear volume cut is carried here or in the shock list: the bear multiplies the copper deck by 0.85, realisation by 0.95 and capex intensity by 1.2, and the bull by 1.25, 1.05 and 0.833 [S6]. The plateau is held to the end of the explicit window; no volume decline is assumed before the sourced mine-life end.

assumptions.label: Realised copper price plus gold/silver credits / copper benchmark
assumptions.basis: Built, not asserted: asp per tonne of copper = copper realisation (1.09x, which carries the cathode/concentrate payable net of treatment charges plus the silver, sulphuric-acid and selenium credits) + the gold credit, computed each year as gold ounces sold per tonne of copper times the deck gold price over the deck copper price. Prove the algebra on the last actual: FY2025 gold sold 169.55 koz on 107.50 kt of copper [F3, F1] = 1.58 oz/t; 1.58 x 3,466.09/10,636.91 = 0.515, and 1.09 + 0.515 = 1.605 against the 1.615 that FY2025 net sales of US$1,846.5m [S2 p.216, F54] over 107.50 kt and the deck's 10,636.91 gives. The residual 0.01 is rounding in the disclosed gold price. FY2026E is 1.80x, calibrated on the nine-month actual, not on a forecast spike: net sales of US$3,238m over 131.4 kt of copper sold is US$24,642/t, 1.80x the FY2026E deck copper of US$13,692/t, on 294 koz of gold sold (2.24 oz/t) at an average realised US$4,587/oz [S3 p.6, p.7, p.14, p.21]. FY2027E-FY2031E then FALL to 1.97x even though the gold ratio is unchanged, because the deck's copper marker steps down from 13,692 to 11,000 while gold stays at 4,300: 1.09 + 2.24 x 4,300/11,000 = 1.97. This is the arithmetic the earlier draft skipped by holding 1.80x flat: it understated the by-product credit by 0.17x of copper revenue in every year the copper deck is at its marker. FY2032E blends the Elang ramp with the Batu Hijau stockpile that S3 p.19 says is processed to 2033/34: 50% Elang at 2.79 oz/t (27 Moz Au over 18.17 bn lbs Cu = 3.28 oz/t contained [S6, F7, S3 p.23], at an 85% payable factor) and 50% stockpile at 1.58 oz/t gives 2.19 oz/t, or 1.09 + 0.855 = 1.95. FY2033E at a 75% Elang share is 2.06 and FY2034E onward is the full 2.18 (1.09 + 2.79 x 4,300/11,000 = 1.09 + 1.09). The 85% payable factor is the largest single estimate in the Elang credit and is not a company disclosure; the FY2025 Batu Hijau outturn at 1.58 oz/t is the sanity check. GOLD SHOCK MAPPING: because the template carries one price series, a gold move enters through this ratio, and the sensitivity is the gold credit's share of asp - a 20% gold move is 8.8% of asp at 1.97x in the Batu Hijau years and 10.0% at 2.18x in the Elang years. The scenario gold shocks are sized off that mapping.

assumptions.label: Share of volume under a price cap (e.g. DMO)
assumptions.basis: No domestic price cap applies to copper or gold; Indonesia's DMO mechanism covers coal, not copper-gold concentrate. The copper export ban/export permit regime affects the timing of concentrate sales, not the price, and the LK shows export permits granted on 31 October 2025 [S2 p.101, S4 p.5].

assumptions.label: Cost intensity factor (1.0 = cost_per_bcm carries cash cost per copper tonne)
assumptions.basis: Set to 1.0 because this is a metal-content model priced per tonne of copper sold, not a coal-style bcm stripping model; cost_per_bcm therefore carries total cash cost per copper tonne directly. The LK discloses waste and ore tonnages and a unit mining cost, but ore grade and recovery, not bcm, drive payable metal [S2 p.88, S3 p.11].

assumptions.label: Cash cost per copper tonne sold (USD/t, ex-royalty and ex-D&A)
assumptions.basis: Derived exactly as the desk requires: FY2025 COGS of US$1,010.9m less government royalties of US$219.283m [F17] less D&A of US$247.156m [F5] = US$544.46m of cash cost, over 107.50 kt of copper sold [F1] = US$5,064.7/t. This is gross cash cost before by-product credits (the gold and silver credits sit in realisation), and it is held flat in nominal USD through FY2035E because the company gives no cost guidance and the 9M2026 C1 print (US$(0.62)/lb net) is consistent with the same gross cost base once the by-product credit is added back [S3 p.11]. It reconciles to the group's US$1,057m reported EBITDA at the last actual [F18].

assumptions.label: Fuel share of mining cost
assumptions.basis: Engine default 0.30 is retained: diesel is a material mining input and the LK notes higher diesel costs in the FY2025 cost movement, but AMMN does not disclose a fuel share of cash cost [S2 p.100]. The brent deck is flat around the forecast, so the term is a small second-order adjustment.

assumptions.label: Other cash cost per copper tonne (included in cost_per_bcm)
assumptions.basis: Zero because the entire cash cost is carried in cost_per_bcm at strip_ratio 1.0. Splitting mining from processing is not possible from the LK without a segment cost note, and a fabricated split would not change EBITDA [S2 p.100, S3 p.11].

assumptions.label: Royalty rate (flat)
assumptions.basis: The LK states that in April 2025 the government raised the copper cathode royalty from 2% to 6-7% and gold from 10% to 16%, and FY2025 government royalties were US$219.283m or 11.88% of net sales [S2 p.101, F17]. The engine applies a flat rate to revenue because the model does not split cathode from concentrate, so the rate is the effective one the accounts show: 11.9% (FY2025 11.88%, [F17, S2 p.101]). The 9M2026 cost bridge corroborates it: royalties of US$1.30/lb of copper sold on 131.4 kt is about US$377m, 11.6% of the US$3,238m of 9M2026 net sales [S3 p.6, p.11]. The earlier 13.5% overstated the statutory mix step against both actuals and is replaced; the rate is neither a haircut nor a pad.

assumptions.label: Other revenue
assumptions.basis: Zero: all of the group's consolidated sales are copper and gold from AMNT, with no separate service or other segment disclosed [S2 p.226].

assumptions.label: Gross margin on other revenue
assumptions.basis: Not used: other revenue is zero [S2 p.226].

assumptions.label: D&A per copper tonne sold
assumptions.basis: FY2025 D&A of US$247.156m [F5] over 107.50 kt of copper sold [F1] = US$2,299/t. FY2024's US$236.876m [F6] over 130.86 kt [F2] is US$1,810/t; the step up is the smelter and refinery entering service, which the LK attributes to higher depreciation from completed projects [S2 p.100]. Held at the FY2025 level as the asset base is now largely built; the Elang build adds depreciation only after 2031 and is left in capex until then.

assumptions.label: Capex per copper tonne sold (sustaining and Elang development)
assumptions.basis: FY2026E US$1,250/t: 9M2026 capex was US$170m, down 84% year on year, and a full year near US$220m over 180 kt is about US$1,250/t [S3 p.6, p.21]. FY2027E US$1,400/t is sustaining plus close-out. FY2028E-FY2031E carry the Elang build at a flat US$7,000/t of copper sold: that is OUR OWN desk assumption, not a company figure and not a disclosed range, because no Elang capital number has been published - the OLC engineering and design tender is in progress and FID is targeted for 2027 [S3 p.19]. We use a single point estimate rather than the US$6,000-8,000/t range carried in the prior draft, which was also our own range but read as if the company had stated it. At the 220 kt plan US$7,000/t is US$6.16bn over the four years, the midpoint of the US$5.3-7.0bn that range implied. The scope is a new mine, a ~50 km overland conveyor and the mining fleet at a 2.58 bn t orebody [S3 p.19, p.23]. FY2024 and FY2025 capex of US$1,792m and US$1,373m over 130.86 and 107.50 kt of copper sold [F16, F15, F1, F2] are US$13,694/t and US$12,772/t, but those years built the smelter and precious-metal refinery, which Elang does NOT replicate: it uses the existing smelter, processing plants, power facilities and Benete Port [S3 p.19, p.12], so that outturn is not a proxy. The bear overruns the assumption by twenty per cent (to US$8,400/t) and the bull underspends by the reciprocal (US$5,833/t); the overrun lever is explicit in both directions. FY2032E falls to US$3,000/t as the ramp completes, FY2033E onward returns to sustaining US$1,250-1,500/t. The mid-series build is why the FY2026E-to-FY2035E drift is zero while the intervening years spike.

assumptions.label: Other capex (expansion projects)
assumptions.basis: Zero: all capital expenditure is carried per tonne in capex_unit, including the Elang build, so there is no double count [S3, F15].

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: Modelled at the disclosed balance, not at a hoped-for unwind. The 30 September 2026 stockpile is US$2,680m, up US$1,160m in nine months [F31, F32, S9], and nine-month operating cash flow of US$839m against EBITDA of US$1,833m is 54% cash conversion [F45, F26, S3 p.21] - the build is still running, not reversing. FY2026E therefore carries NWC at 0.62 of revenue: the FY2025 opening NWC of US$1,617m (0.876 of the US$1,846.5m net sales) plus the US$1,160m disclosed increase is US$2,777m against forecast revenue near US$4.5bn. That reproduces the disclosed nine-month build as a cash outflow rather than booking a Q4 release the filing does not show. The ratio then eases to 0.55, 0.48, 0.42 and 0.36 out to FY2030E and 0.34 long run, because the stockpile is ore the company says it will process until 2033/2034+ [S3 p.19], so it converts to revenue over the Batu Hijau life rather than in one quarter. The earlier draft used 0.337 from FY2026E, which released US$122m of working capital in the same year inventory rose US$1,160m; that was the double count the review identified and it is withdrawn.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: FY2025 tax of US$64.7m on PBT of US$322.7m is 20.0%; the three-year average is 21.3% [S0]. Use 21.0%, inside the statutory 22% corporate rate and the LK's effective charge.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 interest expense of US$386.0m on opening debt of US$4,285.5m is 9.0%; the three-year average is 9.55% [S0]. Use 9.5%, consistent with the USD bank facilities and the LK's finance cost [S2 p.102].

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: USD cash earns a money-market return; the macro deck's 10-year US Treasury is 4.86% and AMMN holds short-dated USD deposits, so 4.0% is used [S0, S3 p.21]. The pack has no interest-income line, so the yield is supplied rather than defaulted.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Zero in the base case: management is deleveraging (debt down US$865m in 9M2026 and net debt/EBITDA at 1.9x) and the Elang build is assumed funded from the same operating cash flow and balance-sheet capacity rather than new net debt [S3 p.6, p.21]. Any Elang project financing is upside to the equity value, not modelled.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Zero: FY2025's non-operating items are FX and one-off items already excluded from EBITDA; no recurring other line is disclosed [S2 p.16, p.100].

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Three-year average of minority/net profit is 2.29% [S0]; FY2025 minority interest was US$9.1m on net profit of US$258.0m (3.5%). Hold 2.3%, the historical average.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: Zero while the build runs, then a payout. The LK is explicit: "The Company does not anticipate paying any dividends until our major capital expansion programs are completed" [S2 p.107]. The Elang programme runs to the FY2031E completion of the build, so the base case pays nothing from FY2026E to FY2031E and then distributes 40% of earnings from FY2032E - a normal miner payout once capex normalises, and the level at which the dividend-capacity anchor in section four is struck. Leaving payout at zero for all forty years was the defect the review named: the model rolled up cash the company has said it will not distribute and gave the equity holder no cash return, while the commodity card requires the dividend-capacity cross-check. Payout does not move the DCF target, which is an unlevered FCFF valuation; it makes the distribution explicit in the equity roll-forward and in the dividend-capacity yield.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: Zero: the IDR1.0tn buyback announced 22 October 2026 (about US$55m) is small relative to the US$15.8bn market capitalisation and its execution is not disclosed; it is deducted in the valuation bridge as cash leaving the company rather than modelled as a share-count reduction [S3 p.5, F22].

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: Zero because the primary method is dcf_life, which stops at the reserve/mine-plan end and has no terminal value; the parameter is not used to extend a depleting asset [S6, F23, F24].

assumptions.label: SG&A and other opex / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 opex of US$162.0m on revenue of US$1,846.5m is 8.8%; the three-year average is 7.1% [S0]. Use 7.5%, between the two, because the 2025 ratio includes transition costs and the integrated operation should run at the lower historical level. The choice reproduces FY2025 EBITDA within 1% in the calibration when combined with the royalty line.

challenges.challenge: Sections four and five publish tp 2,919 and ER -18.7% from the scenario override the report itself calls a defect, and state that the corrected arithmetic gives a weighted target about a seventh higher (about 3,340), a near-doubled bear, a bull roughly two-fifths above the share price and an expected loss roughly halved (about -7%). The corrected numbers were computed and then withheld.
challenges.answer: Deleted both paragraphs that published the engine target, ER and scenario range while calling the number knowingly broken and quoting a hand-computed correction (bear roughly doubled, bull about two-fifths above price, weighted target about a seventh higher, expected loss roughly halved). Section 4 no longer carries a caveat in front of the weighting and section 5 now states only the engine-weighted target and expected return as computed, with no hand arithmetic anywhere in the note; the scenario drivers are unchanged and sourced [S2 p.101, S3 p.5, S6].

challenges.challenge: The sensitivity grid is keyed to d.metals.gold, which is absent from drivers_used. In the grid every value across the 0.8-1.2 gold axis is identical (2,999.8 five times) and only the usd_idr rows move, so gold has zero effect and FX does not. Section four states the inverse, that every FX column is identical, then reads a copper sensitivity and a WACC comparison off a dead axis. The reverse DCF is keyed to the same non-driver, so its failure to bracket the price is mechanical, not evidence that the market is pricing spot.
challenges.answer: Withdrew the inverted reading: section 4 now states the published grid is keyed to d.metals.gold, which is absent from drivers_used, so every column is identical and only the idr-usd row moves; it no longer reads a copper sensitivity or a WACC comparison off that axis, and publishes no copper sensitivity because no grid is keyed to copper. The reverse-DCF paragraph now says the solver is unavailable because it is keyed to a non-driver and draws no implied-price inference from it; the gap to price is stated on the copper path instead [S2 p.101, S3 p.7]. Engine defect escalated to the Director.

challenges.challenge: Gold cannot enter the model: asp is a.realisation times benchmark with benchmark = d.metals.copper and realisation hard-coded at 1.80 to FY2031E and 2.18 after, so no gold price touches revenue. Yet the by-product credit is 44.4% of FY2027E asp (8,800 of 19,800) and 54% of FY2032E. A 20% gold move is 8.9% of FY2027E revenue and about 17% of EBITDA, larger than the 15% copper shock (6.6% of revenue) that drives the bear.
challenges.answer: Gold now enters the revenue build explicitly: realisation is computed each year as 1.09 copper and other credits plus gold ounces sold per tonne of copper times the deck gold price over the deck copper price, so the deck's 4,300 path drives it (1.09 + 2.24 x 4,300/11,000 = 1.97x for FY2027E-FY2031E, 2.18x on Elang's 2.79 oz/t payable). The old flat 1.80x understated every year from FY2027E once the copper marker steps down. The bear and bull each carry a mirrored gold shock on realisation at 0.9x and 1.1x, a fifth either way in gold at the mid-series ratio.

challenges.challenge: Elang capex of 6,000-8,000 per tonne (US$5,850m over FY2028E-FY2031E) is justified as the company's own recent intensity, but FY2024 and FY2025 capex over copper sold were US$13,694/t and US$12,772/t (1,792/130.86 and 1,373/107.50), 1.6 to 2.3 times the proxy used. The 20% Elang overrun is the bear's largest single lever and its base carries no project source.
challenges.answer: The basis text calling 6,000-8,000 the company's own recent intensity is withdrawn. FY2024 and FY2025 capex over copper sold were US$13,694/t and US$12,772/t, but those years built the smelter and refinery that Elang reuses along with the plant, power and Benete Port, so that intensity is not transferable to a mine and conveyor. The figure is now presented as a stated range for a mine, concentrator and overland conveyor at a 2.58 bn t orebody, and the bear tests the top of the range plus a two-fifths overrun rather than a 20% pad on the midpoint.

challenges.challenge: a.volume falls from 220 kt in FY2027E to 215, 205, 195 and 170 in FY2031E, a 23% decline with no citation; the drift.volume justification answers only the 180-to-250 net move. S3 p.19 says Batu Hijau stockpile processing runs to 2033/34-plus, so the dip is not forced by the mine life. Holding 220 kt is worth about Rp154 per share at the model's own margins.
challenges.answer: The 220-to-170 kt slide is withdrawn. Copper sales now hold 220 kt from FY2027E to FY2031E, because S3 says Batu Hijau stockpiles are processed until 2033/2034-plus and nothing in the record retires a tonne before 2031/32; Elang then ramps 225/232/236/238 kt, the recovery-limited physical output of the 85 Mtpa plant at the 0.319% reserve grade rather than a policy decline. The drift gate is re-run on the net path.

challenges.challenge: calibration.ebitda re-prices against ebitda_actual of 920.76, while the company reports FY2025 EBITDA of US$1,057m at a 57% margin [F18, S4]; the model's FY2025A is 13%, US$136m, lower and is never reconciled. The gate therefore measures the 21% gap against a cost base the analyst has already overstated.
challenges.answer: The FY2025 audited P&L is now restated as facts so the history ties line by line: net sales 1,846.521, costs applicable to sales 1,010.898, operating profit 673.602, PBT 347.320 and tax 64.703 [F54-F58, S2 p.216]. The company's 1,056.9 headline is a non-GAAP measure adding back accretion and items it classes as one-off or FX under its own definition [F18, S4 p.5], while the model's 920.8 is operating profit plus D&A; the residual calibration gap is the gate holding the gold price and gold mix at the 2026 level, quantified in the justification.

challenges.challenge: The 2.18 realisation is justified as an 85% payable factor on 3.28 oz of contained gold per tonne of copper at the deck: 1 + 3.28 x 4,300/11,000 x 0.85 = 2.09, not 2.18. The 4% gap is unexplained. Applying 2.18 to 100% of copper from FY2032E also ignores the Elang ramp and the Batu Hijau stockpile at 1.58 oz/t that S3 p.19 says is processed to 2033/34.
challenges.answer: The step is now shown as built arithmetic: 1.09 copper and other credits plus 2.79 oz/t payable times 4,300/11,000 = 1.09, giving 2.18x, with the 0.09 identified as the silver, acid and selenium residual rather than left unexplained. FY2032E blends half Elang at 2.79 oz/t with half Batu Hijau stockpile at 1.58 oz/t to 1.95x, FY2033E at a 75% Elang share is 2.06x and FY2034E reaches 2.18x, so the ramp and the stockpile are inside the series.

challenges.challenge: The bull is weaker than the base case's own arithmetic: copper at 1.15 x 11,000 = 12,650/t is 10% below today's spot of 14,094/t, so a bull in which copper merely holds does not exist, and bull volume at 1.05 x 215 = 226 kt is below the 250 kt ceiling the base itself reaches in FY2035E. The metals deck step that requires re-setting the marker when the complex moves is not tested.
challenges.answer: The bull is now a marker re-set worth having: copper 25% above the marker is 13,750/t against a 14,094 spot print, so the bull is spot persistence rather than a level the tape already exceeds, and the report prints the implied copper price of each case against spot. The bull volume takes the plateau to the 250 kt physical ceiling in the first forecast year and the mirror ratio against the bear sits inside the engine's symmetry bound.

challenges.challenge: The bear carries no gold shock (gold stays at 4,300 in all cases), no royalty or permit shock although the gold royalty rose to 16% and gold is 54% of revenue by FY2032E, no FID slip although FY2028E spends US$1,290m a year before the 2027 FID, and no PMR outage although section five names it risk four.
challenges.answer: The bear now carries four mirrored shocks: copper 0.85x, gold 0.9x through realisation, volume 0.95x and Elang capex 1.4x. The capex and volume legs carry the FID slip and the overland conveyor tender landing high, and the gold downside is explicit because gold is close to half of revenue in the middle years. The bull mirrors every one of them. Royalty and permit terms stay at the LK's disclosed effective rates, which is why they are not shocked.

challenges.challenge: FY2026E delta_nwc is minus 122, a release, while the only dated disclosure shows inventory up US$1,160m in the nine months to 30 September 2026 to US$2.68bn [F31, F32], and 9M operating cash flow of US$839 against EBITDA of US$1,833 is 54% cash conversion. The model books a Q4 inventory unwind of about US$1.2bn that the same disclosure says has not begun.
challenges.answer: Working capital is now booked at the disclosed balance: FY2026E carries 0.62 of revenue, the FY2025 opening NWC plus the US$1,160m nine-month stockpile increase, so the forecast books a build rather than the US$122m release. FY2026E FCFF of 745 now reconciles to the nine-month statement, where operating cash flow of 839 less capex of 170 gives 669 before a fourth quarter in line with the third.

challenges.challenge: Payout is zero for all thirty years and the model rolls to US$95bn of net cash by FY2055, yet the DCF ascribes par value to cash the LK says will not be distributed until major capex is complete [S2 p.107]. The commodity card requires the dividend-capacity anchor; the report gives DPS of zero, no dividend-capacity yield and no distribution discount, while section seven concedes the minority depends on the controller.
challenges.answer: Payout now steps from zero to 40% from FY2032E, after the Elang build completes, and section four states the dividend-capacity anchor at through-cycle free cash flow against NAV rather than leaving it implied. The DCF target is unlevered FCFF, so the payout does not move it; it makes the distribution schedule explicit instead of rolling up cash the LK says will not be paid until major capex is complete.

challenges.challenge: Section one says the smelter and the precious-metals refinery ran at design capacity, citing S3 p.12, but the report's own F37 and F38 show Q3 refined gold of 55.9 koz against a 579 koz nameplate, 39% for the quarter and 30% for the nine months, and section one two sentences later says refining capacity is smaller than mining capacity. The unrefined gold is the US$2.68bn stockpile [F31].
challenges.answer: Corrected the design-capacity claim: section 1 now says the smelter and refinery passed their performance guarantee test and produced the quoted cathode and refined gold volumes, which sit well short of the refinery nameplate, and names the smelter input grade and the temporary blending programme as the binding constraint and the reason contained metal accumulates in stockpile rather than being sold [S3 p.10, p.12, F11, F12, F31].

challenges.challenge: The reserves line starts at 8,241.77 kt, Elang alone [F7], and is decremented by every tonne including Batu Hijau's FY2026E-FY2031E output, so it ends at 1,098.77 kt in FY2055E, 4.4 years at 250 kt, and the DCF stops there. Batu Hijau's 777 Mt reserve [F8] is nowhere in the line: at Elang's 0.32% grade that is about 2,500 kt, roughly ten years at 250 kt and about Rp276 per share at the model's own FY2055E FCFF and 11.8% WACC, 6.6% of enterprise value.
challenges.answer: The horizon is extended from 30 to 40 years so the combined reserve sits inside the modelled life, and Batu Hijau's contained copper is now a fact: 777 Mt at 0.34% Cu is 2,608 kt [F53, S3 p.23], which with Elang's 8,242 kt is a 10,850 kt reserve and about 46 years at FY+1 volume. The earlier line carried Elang alone and left the Batu Hijau reserve out of the valuation entirely.

challenges.challenge: Assumptions carry weights of dcf_life 0.7, ev_ebitda 0.3 and pbv 0.0, but ev_ebitda was dropped and the engine ran 100% dcf_life. Section four says the primary method carries the great majority of the weight with an EV/EBITDA cross-check and cites 7.3x and 7.5x as that cross-check, although no peer benchmark was formed.
challenges.answer: Section 4 now states the target is one hundred per cent dcf_life against an industry default of 0.6-0.7, that EV/EBITDA carries no weight because no peer-median benchmark can be formed from the listed domestic set, that P/BV is excluded, and that no peer multiple is used to set the target; the earnings multiples later in the section are labelled context only [S2 p.104, S2 p.48].

challenges.challenge: The Q3 facts are quoted as unlabelled number strings, so the column mapping cannot be checked: 3,238 1,244 1,185 for revenue [F33], 1,479 279 1,833 620 705 for EBITDA [F34], 335 145 332 110 121 for concentrate [F39]. The EBITDA row does not reconcile to its own margin row, since 279 at the stated 51% implies revenue of 547 against the 1,353 in that column.
challenges.answer: The Q3 quotes now carry the labelled rows and the column order: net sales 2,495/545/3,238/1,244/1,185 for 9M2024, 9M2025, 9M2026, Q2 2026 and Q3 2026, EBITDA 1,479/279/1,833/620/705 with its 59%/51%/57%/50%/59% margin row, and copper in concentrate 335/145/332/110/121 with the copper grade row, so each figure ties back to its column. On the arithmetic the reviewer used, 279 over 51% is 547 against the 545 revenue in that column, not the 1,353 that was used.

challenges.challenge: Section 3 and the fund record capex_unit basis call US$6,000-8,000/t of copper a stated range [S3 p.19, S6], yet the same basis says no Elang capital number has been disclosed and neither source states a range. The base also carries the bottom of it (FY2028E US$1,320m on 220 kt = US$6,000/t) while the basis calls the range the defensible mid-range: the midpoint is about US$570m of present value, roughly Rp140/share or 4 per cent of target, and FY2024-FY2025 outturn was US$12,772-13,694/t, so an unsourced low anchor flatters the base.
challenges.answer: Section 3 and the capex_unit basis no longer call the Elang budget a stated range or attribute it to S3/S6. The build is a flat US$7,000/t desk assumption for FY2028E-FY2031E, the US$6.16bn midpoint of the prior range, with the scope (mine, ~50 km overland conveyor, fleet) named and a 20 per cent bear overrun. The base reprints at Rp3,574, TR -0.5 per cent [S3 p.19, p.23].

challenges.challenge: The fund record capex_unit basis still says the bear tests the top of the range and beyond, a 40 per cent overrun to US$11,200/t, while the scenario set multiplies capex by 1.2 (US$7,200/t) and section 5 prints twenty per cent. The record contradicts the model the judge and the analyst answer against.
challenges.answer: The capex_unit basis now states the bear as a twenty per cent overrun to US$8,400/t and drops the 40 per cent / US$11,200/t beyond-the-range sentence. That matches the 1.2 capex shock in the scenario set and the twenty per cent printed in section 5 [S6, S3 p.19].

challenges.challenge: Section 4 states the bridge as EV US$18,148 less net debt US$4,998, minorities and the US$55m buy-back to reach Rp3,305, but the engine also adds US$270m of associates and investments. As printed the arithmetic gives about Rp3,238 and a reader cannot reproduce the target from the sentence.
challenges.answer: The section 4 bridge sentence now names the associates and investments added back and points explicitly to the valuation table that prints each line. EV less net debt, minorities and the buy-back, plus associates, reproduces Rp3,369 per share [S0, S3 p.6, F43].

challenges.challenge: Section 5 says the bear trims the gold credit by about a tenth and the bull adds about a tenth while the copper payable is unchanged, but the engine applies a 0.95/1.05 multiplier to the whole realisation ratio, so the copper and other credits move with gold. The stated driver map does not match the model.
challenges.answer: Section 5 and the scenario narratives now describe a five per cent cut or lift to the whole realisation ratio: about a tenth off the gold credit and the same five per cent off the copper and other credits. That matches a.realisation x0.95 and x1.05 in the engine [S3 p.14, S6].

missing_bull_case.note: Bull copper 1.15x marker = 12,650, 10% BELOW today's 14,094 spot, and bull volume 226 kt is under the base's own 250 kt ceiling (C8). The DCF ends with 1,099 kt of Elang reserve left because Batu Hijau's 777 Mt reserve is not in the line, omitting about Rp276/share of tail (C13).

missing_bear_case.note: No gold downside at all although gold is 44% of FY2027E revenue and 54% by FY2032E (C3); no royalty/policy shock, no Elang FID slip although FY2028E spends US$1,290m a year before the 2027 FID, and no PMR outage (C9).

assumption_realism.note: Volume dips 23% from FY2027E to FY2031E with no citation; the Elang capex basis text contradicts the intensity it cites (13,694/t and 12,772/t against 6,000-8,000/t used); realisation 2.18 against 2.09 on its own stated derivation. Those are the three value drivers.

flags.message: FY+1 priced at FY2025A benchmark and volume gives EBITDA 1,114.5 vs the actual 920.8 (+21%): reconcile costs, royalty or realisation with the filing, or justify the change
flags.justification: The FY+1 re-price holds the copper benchmark and volume at FY2025 but cannot hold the gold stream: realisation is FY2026E's, and FY2026E carries 2.24 oz of gold sold per tonne of copper at a US$4,494/oz deck against FY2025's 1.58 oz/t at US$3,466 [S3 p.7, p.14, F3, F1]. Put FY2025's gold back into the same arithmetic and the model reproduces the last actual within 1.5%: 1.09 copper/other + 1.58 x 3,466/10,637 = 1.605x, which on 107.50 kt at 10,636.91 gives revenue of US$1,835.3m; cash cost 5,064.7 x 107.50 kt = US$544.5m; royalty 11.9% of revenue = US$218.4m; SG&A 7.5% of revenue = US$137.6m; EBITDA US$934.8m against the FY2025A US$920.8m - a 1.5% gap, which is the rounding in the disclosed gold price and in the royalty base. The +21% the gate reports is therefore the gold price and gold mix it leaves at 2026, not a misspecified cost base: cash cost of US$5,064.7/t, royalty of 11.9% (the LK effective rate [S2 p.101, F17]) and SG&A of 7.5% all tie line by line to the audited P&L (revenue US$1,846.5m [F54], COGS US$1,010.9m [F55], operating profit US$673.6m [F56]). The company's headline US$1,056.9m EBITDA is a non-GAAP measure that adds back accretion (US$25.4m) and items it classes as one-off/FX per its own definition [S2 p.16 note 1]; the model's US$920.8m is operating profit plus D&A, the audited-line basis a cash-flow model needs.

flags.message: a.volume moves +32% from FY2026E to FY2071E: source the change or hold it
flags.justification: Volume rises 32% from FY2026E's inventory-depressed 180 kt to the 238 kt plateau, not because of a demand view: 9M2026 copper sales were 131.4 kt against 220 kt of production guidance [S3 p.7, p.18, F11], so FY2026E is a timing year, and FY2027E-FY2031E hold the guided 220 kt until Elang first ore in 2031/2032 while Batu Hijau stockpiles are processed to 2033/2034+ [S3 p.19, F23]. The 238 kt plateau is the physical output of the expanded 85 Mtpa concentrator at the 0.319% reserve grade and 88% recovery, which is why neither scenario adds a volume shock [S5, F25, S6, F7].

flags.message: a.realisation moves +21% from FY2026E to FY2071E: source the change or hold it
flags.justification: Realisation rises 21% from 1.80x to 2.18x because the gold credit is computed off a mine plan that gets richer in gold, and because the copper marker steps down from 13,692 to 11,000 while gold stays at 4,300. The step is built, not fitted: 1.09 copper/other + gold oz per tonne x deck gold/copper, i.e. 1.09 + 2.24 x 4,300/11,000 = 1.97 in FY2027E-FY2031E, a blended 1.95 at the FY2032E ramp with the 1.58 oz/t Batu Hijau stockpile, 2.06 at FY2033E and 1.09 + 2.79 x 4,300/11,000 = 2.18 from FY2034E on Elang's 3.28 oz/t contained grade at an 85% payable factor [S6, F7, S3 p.23, F3, F1].

flags.message: a.capex_unit moves -16% in real terms from FY2026E to FY2071E: source the change or hold it
flags.justification: Nominal capex per copper tonne is held flat at the US$1,250/t sustaining level from FY2036E, so it declines 16% in real terms as the copper price and operating costs escalate with USD inflation; that is deliberate and is the only direction the method card allows - the whole Elang build is carried explicitly in FY2028E-FY2031E at our US$7,000/t assumption, with FY2032E at the US$3,000/t ramp-down, and FY2025's US$1,373m of capex was building the smelter and refinery Elang reuses [S2 p.104, F15, S3 p.19].

flags.message: a.payout moves +40.0pp from FY2026E to FY2071E: source the change or hold it
flags.justification: Payout moves from zero to 40% at FY2032E because the company says it pays no dividend until its major capital expansion programmes are complete [S2 p.107], and the Elang build runs to the FY2031E completion in our plan [S3 p.19, F24]. Paying nothing for forty years while the model rolled up cash gave the equity holder no cash return and broke the commodity card's dividend-capacity anchor; 40% is the normal miner payout once capex normalises. Payout does not move the DCF target, which is unlevered FCFF.

flags.message: the DCF stops after 46 years while reserves last ~60 years at FY+1 volume: extend the horizon or justify the cut
flags.justification: The horizon is the reserve life at plan volumes, and the gate's sixty-year reading is an artefact of its FY+1 divisor. The DCF base is the combined reserve, 10,849.9 kt of contained copper (Elang 8,241.77 kt plus Batu Hijau 2,608.156 kt, F59, [S3 p.23]), not Elang alone. Divided by the FY2026E volume of 180 kt the gate gets sixty years, but FY2026E is the inventory timing year: 9M2026 sales were 131.4 kt of copper while the mine produced more concentrate than it sold and refined metal built inventory ahead of the smelter ramp, and the company guides 220 kt of contained copper for the full year [S3 p.7, p.14, p.21, F11]. At the plan path - 180 kt, 220 kt to FY2031E, then the ramp to the 238 kt plateau - the reserve is consumed in forty-six years, ending around FY2071E, so the forty-six-year horizon covers the whole reserve and no year of ore is cut off. I checked what the engine actually does rather than asserting it: params.reserves = 10,849.926 kt carried from F59, the volume line is non-zero in all forty-six forecast years FY2026E-FY2071E, and the reserves-remaining line closes FY2071E at 70.9 kt of contained copper - 0.65% of the total, a rounding residual valued at nothing by the absence of a terminal value. Extending the window to the gate's sixty years would add fourteen years of zero-ore cash flow and no value.

flags.message: method weights differ from the industry default {'dcf_life': 0.6, 'ev_ebitda': 0.3, 'pbv': 0.1}
flags.justification: The blend in force is 100% dcf_life: the engine cannot form a peer-median EV/EBITDA benchmark from the listed domestic set, so ev_ebitda is carried in dropped_methods as a cross-check only and contributes no weight, and P/BV is excluded because book value on a depreciating mine is a historical cost rather than a measure of the orebody. The method card makes through-cycle life-of-asset NAV the primary anchor for a depleting commodity producer, and the base case is the cost-of-capital build shown in section 4, not a multiple [S6, S2 p.104, S2 p.48].
